Closes #2148

Turn-end finalization rewrites every checkpoint created during the turn with the full transcript, and each rewrite can fetch refs and blobs from the remote. Each fetch has its own limit, and the dead-network memos stop a fully unavailable remote from costing that limit once per checkpoint. Nothing bounded the pass as a whole, though: a slow but responsive remote finishes every fetch just under its limit, trips neither memo, and lets the total outlast the host's hook timeout. The host then kills the hook before session state is saved, leaving checkpoints with provisional transcripts and only warning logs to explain it.

## The fix

The network phase of `finalizeAllTurnCheckpoints` (the checkpoint store open and the write loop) now runs under a deadline derived from the real limit the agent's host places on the turn-end hook.

**Only the network phase checks the deadline.** Reading, sanitizing, externalizing and redacting the transcript is local work that never checks the context, so it is never interrupted part-way. Its time still counts against the budget: if it runs long, finalize gives up at the first network step instead of starting fetches the hook has no time to finish. The deadline is checked again after the store opens, so precompute does not hash the transcript for writes that will never start. A write that fails as the deadline passes logs its error before it is counted as an interruption.

**The deadline is `processStart` plus a per-agent budget**, the same pattern `sessionEndCondenseDeadline` uses. The host measures its timeout from when it spawned the hook, so Entire measures from process start too.

**Each agent derives its budget from its own hook timeout** through a new `agent.TurnEndBudgeter` capability, so a change to the timeout carries the budget with it (#1237 just changed Claude Code's). `agent.TurnEndBudgetWithin` keeps a fifth of the timeout, between 2s and 10s, as headroom for the state save after finalize.

| Agent | Turn-end hook limit | Source | Budget |
|---|---|---|---|
| Claude Code | 120s | `checkpointHookTimeoutSec` | 110s |
| Antigravity | 300s | `stopHookTimeoutSeconds` | 290s |
| Factory AI Droid | 60s | Host default ([docs](https://docs.factory.com/reference/hooks-reference)) | 50s |
| Codex | 30s | `defaultHookTimeoutSec` | 24s |
| Copilot CLI | 30s | Host default ([docs](https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/reference/hooks-configuration)) | 24s |
| Pi | 10s | The extension's `execFile` timeout, pinned by a test | 8s |
| Cursor, OpenCode, Vogon, external agents | Unknown or none | `defaultTurnEndHookTimeout` (30s) | 24s |

`TestTurnEndBudgetLedger` requires every built-in agent to either declare a budget or appear in `turnEndBudgetFallbacks` with a reason, and fails on a stale entry. A new agent cannot silently inherit the default. External agents always take the default, since the protocol carries no hook timeout.

## When finalization is cut short

- Checkpoints already rewritten keep the full transcript; the rest keep their provisional one.
- **This is permanent.** Turn start clears `TurnCheckpointIDs`, and nothing revisits a finalize, so there is no retry. That is the tradeoff for the hook finishing inside its host's limit.
- `CaptureDegradedAt` is set, so `entire status` reports it. This now also covers the host cancelling the hook (SIGTERM ends the root context), which used to be silent.
- The interruption is recorded where it is observed, not inferred afterwards. The two exits that keep IDs for a repeated Stop (late transcript, degraded scanner) run before the network phase and keep them regardless of the deadline. An ordinary write error is not reported as degradation. One older path also keeps the IDs; see "Not included".
- Cut-off checkpoints are reported once, as capture degradation, not also as finalize errors.

## Decision for reviewers

**The 30s fallback** is a judgment call. Cursor documents only a "platform default". OpenCode applies no limit: Entire's plugin runs the hook through `spawnSync`, which blocks OpenCode's UI until `entire` exits, so the fallback is also the only bound OpenCode has. 30s matches the limit Codex and Copilot enforce. It is one constant in `lifecycle.go`.

## Verification

- Tests cover:
  - no deadline, a future deadline, and slow fetches without a deadline: all checkpoints finalize
  - a deadline passed before the network phase, the deadline expiring mid-loop while the parent context stays alive, the context ending mid-loop, and the parent cancelled before start: the right checkpoints stay provisional, degradation is recorded, and no error is counted
  - an ordinary write error: no degradation
  - the degraded-scanner and late-transcript exits: they keep their IDs under an expired deadline
  - every agent's budget: derived from, and below, its declared timeout
  - Pi's Go constant: matches the `.ts` file
  - the ledger
- The parent-cancel mid-loop case is deterministic: the fake fetcher ends the context itself. The deadline mid-loop case has its second fetch block until the deadline fires, with a 10s fallback so a regression fails instead of hanging. Its deadline is 3s because it also covers transcript preparation and the store open, so a slow runner still reaches the first fetch.
- Each new test was checked against a planted regression (the deadline starting at the top, the writes ignoring the deadline, cancellation not flagged, Pi's constant drifting, a missing or stale ledger entry) and failed each time.
- `mise run fmt && mise run lint`: 0 issues.
- `mise run test:ci`: two kinds of failure, neither from this change:
  - `TestPreviewNextCheckpoint` and three `TestCheckpointListPending_Preview*` tests also fail on a clean `main`. Their fixtures hardcode 2026-10-07 and began failing seven days later.
  - Load-sensitive tests time out under the full parallel run and pass on their own: `TestExternalCommand_SigintReachesPlugin` on one run, and `TestInstallHooks_ForeignWrapperOverPreGuardEntireDoesNotRecurse` and `TestInstallHooks_ReclaimedChainRunsEachHookOnce` on another.

## Not included

- No durable retry queue for cut-off checkpoints.
- No change to the per-fetch budgets, and no batching of missing-blob fetches.
- No explicit timeout written into Cursor's hook config. That would replace the fallback with a known limit, but changing Entire's hook config needs a doctor repair to reach existing installs, so it is a separate change.
- Local turn-end work counts against the budget, since the clock starts at process start like the host's. For an agent whose host applies no limit, such as OpenCode, finalize can now give up on checkpoints that used to finish when local work runs long. A longer default for agents known to have no limit would avoid that. Follow-up.
- If the checkpoint store fails to open for a reason other than the deadline, finalize still returns with `TurnCheckpointIDs` set and without recording capture degradation. This predates this change. Follow-up.
